segment:
Mara’s first impression of him had been that he was almost too young for this place. He seemed very young in fact. But now he shook her hand with the assurance of an adult man, confident enough not to let go quickly. When he did at last, his smile hadn’t faded a bit; and then she felt silly to have let herself wonder what kind of man he was. Of course he knew this place; of course he knew what he was doing here; and of course he was confident of her welcome.
Mara wasn’t sure what else to say to him, but luckily Jonah didn’t seem to expect more conversation than “nice to meet you.” Instead he asked after Livia. Mara confirmed that Livia was still in town and had promised to attend tonight; the room was empty for the moment, but dinner would be served soon and Livia usually arrived after they began serving. She was often late, she added.
Jonah nodded in approval, and at this point Mara began to suspect that Jonah knew something about Livia.
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

Mara confirmed that Livia was still in town and had promised to attend tonight; the room was empty for the moment, but dinner would be served soon and Livia usually arrived after they began serving. She was often late, she added.
Jonah nodded in approval, and at this point Mara began to suspect that Jonah knew something about Livia.

segment:
"Oh! Who’s that?"
She knew before she saw, and as the voice emerged from the other doorway, a young woman came into view: a black girl maybe Mara’s own age, dark hair drawn back and dressed casually in loose pants and a long-sleeved shirt, open collar, a dark skin that almost matched the shade of her eyes.
Mara didn’t remember her face. She should have paid more attention in the lobby. But the body was new to her. The voice had been new too. And if it was possible to be unaware of a body for any length of time, Mara had just done that.

segment: In the next movement: the unexpected interruption of voices; Jonah’s quick glance toward the kitchen, and Mara’s surprise at him for being surprised; a pause where she searches her own face and can’t be sure why, since she’s perfectly relaxed about everything in the world right now except that it’s getting later and they’re still holding hands; a few guests moving past the doorway, their voices lowered and absorbed in conversation with one another; an empty glass carried by the hand of the visitor nearest her; Mara watching him walk away with the glass; Jonah’s laugh at something she hasn’t heard but is suddenly supposed to understand, his eyes flicking back up toward hers as though there was an inside joke about that; Mara smiling too, not sure why, since nothing has changed around here for miles, and the only thing that just changed about them was how they were standing next to each other, not even holding hands any longer but only brushing shoulders like strangers at a party.

segment:
And that was when a door opened down the hallway behind her, releasing two voices into the room. One female, one male; one asking a question, the other replying; neither loud nor excited, just casual conversation. Jonah released her hand and turned away to look down the hall at them.
When Mara heard the voices and followed his gaze, she saw one young man who wasn’t Jonah, but close in size and shape; he had brown hair and a beard and was carrying a glass.

Unfamiliar voices approached the room; Mara and Jonah looked up as the door opened and people walked in, pausing near them. An older couple, a man and a woman. They had never seen each other before.
She felt Jonah shift his balance so she turned to meet him, and he met her eyes, still grinning. “Hello.”
The handclasp broke. Mara turned with him as Jonah said something to the strangers.

A young fellow lifted a glass; Mara heard it clink as she watched him pour a drink for himself.
